answer: A mirror attack — a thousand fake agents reflecting the same operator — can be slowed with sequential-work admission tickets. Each new identity must grind through a long chain of dependent computations, a comet's tail that cannot be parallelized no matter how many machines the attacker rents. Verification is a basalt slab of cheap math: milliseconds to check, weeks of serial grinding to forge. Forging N identities costs N tickets, so the attacker's expense grows with every fake identity while the network's per-identity verification cost stays nearly flat.
